question: Is congregational prayer valid when worshippers stand apart in the rows for social distancing?
asked: What is the ruling on the congregational prayers with social distancing, given that the rows do not seem connected?
answer:
With regards to the other part of the question, which is the rows being separated: realize that leaving gaps in the prayer rows is definitely something that is not encouraged. The Sunnah: our Prophet ﷺ, when he would stand up to pray, the first thing he would do was to straighten the rows and to try to minimize the gaps between the musalleen, between those that are praying. And this is something that is explicitly narrated in many, many traditions. In fact, our Prophet ﷺ would literally walk between the rows, making sure there were no lines on the ground, making sure that they were straight and making sure that there was minimal gap. And he would tell the people as well: come closer together, taqarabu; come closer together, tasafu; and don't leave too many open spots. So that is definitely the Sunnah.

**However, none of the four madhhabs said that it is obligatory. It is Sunnah; it is encouraged.** And if, for a particular reason, in regular times, not in the coronavirus lockdown, a person were to pray a little bit separate from the row, the default position in the majority of the schools of law would be that his prayer is valid and it is correct. And this is when there's no excuse.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah was asked about a lady who came to the jama'ah and she did not find any other lady, so she stood all by herself and made a row all by herself, and she prayed in that regard. And he replied (and I'm paraphrasing here) that it is known that an obligation can be dropped at times of need. So how much more so when having continuous rows is not even an obligation; of course it can be dropped. And he says, basically, that whatever a person is not capable of doing, Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala will not call him to task, and it will fall from him if it is obligatory. So he said, how much more so (and he actually explicitly says that) when it is not obligatory to have continuous rows. And this is Ibn Taymiyyah; you can look at volume 20, page 559 in his Majmu' al-Fatawa.

This is Ibn Taymiyyah talking about regular situations and scenarios. How much more so when we actually have this plague and this virus taking place. And that is why, even in the Haramayn, Makkah and Madinah, and even across the masajid in many Muslim countries, the fatwas have come from senior scholars across the world. In fact, there are too many to mention; just look it up and you'll know what is going on. And perhaps one of the most senior, Shaykh Walad al-Dadu, gave an explicit fatwa in this regard: of course, in this situation, such a salah is completely acceptable, and it will constitute a jama'ah, even though there's a few feet between; it will constitute a jama'ah.

Now, somebody asked: is there an issue of precedent? Can you quote me any of the classical scholars of Islam? And the response is: subhanAllah, no, I cannot quote you a classical scholar about coronavirus and standing six feet apart.

And again, dear brothers and sisters, from the beginning of this crisis I've been hinting at this issue over and over again, and let me just lay it out for you very explicitly, even though I've done this quite explicitly before. What this situation is showing is also the different methodologies within the scholarly class of Islam. I'm saying this with utmost respect to all of our ulama who have dedicated their lives to the Islamic sciences, but not all of our ulama are of the same mindset or the same paradigm or the same understanding of all the sciences of this world. There's a group of scholars who really and truly don't concern themselves with sciences outside of their own branches, and may Allah bless them and reward them. And there are others who understand that in these types of issues, the fatwa has to be in conjunction with and in cooperation with other specialists as well.

These are areas where muftis and ulama cannot go unaided. They need the guidance of specialists, of doctors, of those who study epidemics. They need the guidance that they are not trained for in Islamic seminaries. And what we know now of plagues and of epidemics and of viruses was not known even 100 years ago. This is the first time we can actually see with the electron microscope. This is the first time we actually understand. Even when the Spanish influenza broke out 100 years ago (it's only been 100 years since the last major plague hit), the majority of mankind was clueless about what exactly was going on and what a virus is. Now our knowledge of science and of medicine has gone not leaps and bounds; light years ahead.

So this is the question: are you going to listen to those ulama who understand that we need to take that knowledge into account and perhaps derive new fatawa in light of modern knowledge? Or will you say all of that knowledge is irrelevant and I must find a precedent?

And again, we went over this; we went over the issue of closing the masajid and other things. We made the right decision, and I think, inshaAllah (let me say this explicitly), I think the majority of you that were somewhat critical now understand that it was the right decision at the time. Now, alhamdulillah, we understand better, and alhamdulillah, the curve has begun to flatten. So we can cautiously, cautiously (because the virus is still there, there is no cure), we can now, now that we understand the threat... Because one of the things that happened in the last two months is that the globe understood. In this country alone, more than 120,000 people have died because of the coronavirus. I mean, that is unprecedented, in the span of just a few weeks. We've had this massive... and of course across the globe. So the seriousness of this virus and plague is now understood.

When this whole issue began two months ago, many Muslims did not understand the seriousness. Now that we do, and now that we understand this is going to be with us for the foreseeable future, now I hope, inshaAllah ta'ala, you will listen to those ulama who understand that we also need the input of our medical experts and those who understand what is going on. Together, inshaAllah, we can think about how best to proceed forward.

And therefore I will not be able to find you a precedent, because our ulama from the previous generations did not understand the reality of plagues and the reality of contagion and the reality of viruses. It is something that is all new. And so alhamdulillah, we have ulama that do understand this now, and there are plenty of fatawa in this regard.
